sessions.summary: Okay, let’s wrap up. It sounds like you were feeling worried (55/100) when facing a lot of projects and feeling unsure about your skills, leading to the thought “I have no ability.” We explored how you *were* able to use AI to bring your ideas to life, which is a valuable skill in itself. It seems recognizing this helped you shift your perspective, and your worry has decreased to 45/100. You identified magnification as a thinking pattern at play. Your balanced thought – “Because I have so much work to do, using ai is acceptable, and I can also learn something in the process” – acknowledges the situation and finds a more helpful way to view your abilities. Good work completing this thought record – it takes effort to step back and reflect like this.

llm_summary: This record shows a shift from feeling worried (55/100) to feeling somewhat less worried (45/100) when encountering a heavy workload and self-doubt regarding skills. The initial automatic thought, "I have no ability," was challenged by recognizing the positive aspects of utilizing AI – framing it not as a deficit, but as a practical skill and a means of bringing ideas to fruition. Identifying magnification as a distortion was a key step in reframing the situation. Developing the balanced thought acknowledged both the workload and the usefulness of AI, allowing for a more compassionate self-assessment. This illustrates the power of identifying and adjusting unhelpful thought patterns to better manage challenging feelings.
llm_action_items: Continue identifying evidence *for* and *against* automatic thoughts.
Practice labeling thought distortions as they arise in daily life.
Reflect on situations where utilizing tools (like AI) supported successful outcomes.
